question: Which of the following correctly shows the relationship between magnification (M) , the object distances (u) and image- distance (v) ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnification = v/u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Magnification** is a measure of how much larger or smaller the image of an object appears compared to the object itself.
 
• The formula for magnification is given by: **M = v/u**, where:
 
 
• **M** is the magnification,
 
• **v** is the image distance (distance of the image from the optical center),
 
• **u** is the object distance (distance of the object from the optical center).
 
 
 
• **Correct Option:** Magnification = v/u.
 
• Magnification can be:
 
 
• **Positive**: When the image is upright (virtual image).
 
• **Negative**: When the image is inverted (real image).
 
 
 
• Other options like Magnification = u + v, Magnification = v × u, and Magnification = u/v are incorrect as they do not represent the correct mathematical relationship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Magnification and Image Formation:**

 
 
• Magnification tells us about the relative size of the image compared to the object.
 
• If **|M| > 1**, the image is magnified (larger than the object).
 
• If **|M| 
 
 
• **Nature of the Image:**
 
 
• For convex lenses, a real and inverted image has a negative magnification.
 
• For concave lenses, a virtual and upright image has a positive magnification.
 
 
 
• **Lens Formula:** The magnification formula is closely related to the lens formula: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u, where f is the focal length of the lens.
 
• **Applications of Magnification:**
 
 
• Used in microscopes, telescopes, and magnifying glasses to enlarge small objects.
 
• Essential in optics for designing lenses and optical instruments.
 
 
 
• **Understanding Incorrect Options:**
 
 
• **Magnification = u + v:** This is mathematically incorrect as magnification depends on the ratio of image and object distances, not their sum.
 
• **Magnification = v × u:** This is also incorrect as there is no product relationship between v and u in magnification.
 
• **Magnification = u/v:** This is the inverse of the correct formula and does not represent the actual relationship.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sign Convention in Optics:**

 
 
• Distances measured against the direction of incident light are negative.
 
• Distances measured in the direction of incident light are positive.
 
• Height of the image is positive if it is above the principal axis and negative if below it.
 
 
 
• **Practical Implications:**
 
 
• Magnification helps in designing optical instruments like cameras, projectors, and eyeglasses.
 
• It is a critical factor in medical imaging systems like endoscopes.
